mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months raises the cost of capital, depressing corporate earnings growth and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A strong, sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (with UNRATE below 4.5%) over three months indicates labor market expansion without overheating, which supports corporate earnings and consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for 3 months AND UNRATE < 4.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly positive at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals increased consumer spending financed by debt, which temporarily boosts demand but raises default risk, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days before reverting.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly positive at 5% significance.
